newsitem.title: USA: Union Pacific clears NGL from ruptured line.
newsitem.headline: Union Pacific clears NGL from ruptured line.

text.p: Union Pacific Resources Group crews on Friday were working to remove residual natural gas liquids from a 10-inch pipeline ruptured a day earlier by a construction crew, company officials said.

The rupture Thursday morning forced the evacuation of 285 people from a rural section of Liberty County near Rye, Texas north of Houston. There were no injuries and residents were expected to be able to return home later today.

The pipeline, which was ruptured by a construction crew laying a parallel pipe under a creek bed, moves liquids between Carthage, Texas and an Enterprise refinery at Mont Belvieu on the Texas coast, company officials said.

The Fort Worth-based Union Pacific Resources moves ethane, propane and butane on the line, and diverted shipments from the 25,000 barrel per day pipeline onto a nearby Chevron pipeline about eight hours after the rupture.

Blow-down valves were used to flare off liquids and depressurize an eight mile section of the line overnight. Repairs were expected to take about two weeks because the pipe was ruptured about 50 feet below a creek bed, a company spokesman told Reuters.
